records.summary: A 1 kg gimbal rated for 2 kg that carries a light mirrorless camera, a compact, an action camera or a phone, with a built-in tracking camera and a detachable 1.3-inch touchscreen remote that works up to 12 m away. Digital Camera World gave it five stars in July 2025.
records.fit: Suits solo creators with a light mirrorless body and a short zoom who also want one gimbal for a phone or action camera. Anyone with a full-frame body and an f/2.8 zoom should look at FeiyuTech's SCORP 3 ($299 on FeiyuTech's store, 3.5 kg payload) instead.
caveats: Digital Camera World's George Cairns (July 2025, tested with iPhones only) found the AI tracker left too much headroom and overrode his own joystick framing.
With a camera mounted it tracks faces only, started by hand gesture; picking another object to track works only with a phone in the Feiyu ON app, and only one subject at a time (FeiyuTech FAQ).
FeiyuTech limits lenses to 90 mm long and 75 mm wide for proper balance; Insta360 Ace Pro 2 can be stabilized but not controlled.
Store reviewers report a learning curve for balancing and thin setup instructions, and one says the phone mount clashes with iPhone 18 Pro buttons.
$207.20 is FeiyuTech's Black Friday price (sale runs Nov 16–30); the product page shows $259 before the sale.

records.summary: FeiyuTech's full-size camera gimbal, rated for 3.5 kg, with a detachable touchscreen remote and a built-in face-tracking camera started by hand gestures. Digital Camera World rated it level with DJI's RS 4, which is rated for 3 kg.
records.fit: Suits shooters with a full-frame mirrorless or DSLR body and a standard f/2.8 zoom who want 14-hour battery life and Arca-type plates. Phone shooters and owners of light APS-C kits should take the SCORP Mini 3 Pro ($207.20 on FeiyuTech's store), and anyone who needs object tracking should look at Hohem's iSteady MT3 Pro ($314.99 on Hohem's store).
caveats: Camera only: no phone holder, and the tracker follows faces by hand gesture with no object tracking (FeiyuTech FAQ).
Digital Camera World's George Cairns (Sept 2025, Sony A7 III with Tamron 28-75mm, 1.37 kg) found it a little wobbly at speed and on low-angle walking shots, and balancing took him 5–10 minutes.
At about 1.4 kg it is heavier than the SCORP 2 (1,070 g).
A store reviewer reports the trigger only switches modes when the gimbal is held still, which FeiyuTech support told him is by design.
Not waterproof; FeiyuTech advises against rain or very humid conditions.
$299 is FeiyuTech's Black Friday price (sale runs Nov 16–30); the product page shows $399 before the sale.

records.summary: A 335 g folding 3-axis phone gimbal with a built-in 8.5-inch extension rod and about 6.5 hours of battery. At $59 on FeiyuTech's store it is half its $119 list price.
records.fit: Suits casual phone videographers who want a cheap, folding stabilizer that doubles as a selfie stick. Anyone who wants tracking without the app, or a full 360° pan, should look at Hohem's iSteady V3 Ultra ($124.99 on Hohem's store at its Black Friday price).
caveats: The AI tracking module is not in the box; without it, tracking runs through the Feiyu ON app, and FeiyuTech's VB4 Kit bundle that includes it is sold out.
Pan is limited to -80° to +185°, not a full 360° rotation.

The product page headline says it fits iPhone 17/16/15/14 Pro, but the compatibility list on the same page stops at iPhone 15 and Galaxy S23; check the phone's weight (260 g max) and width (88 mm max).
No independent review of the VB4 was found; its 12 reviews on FeiyuTech's store average 5.0, and several say setup takes practice.
$59 is a sale price against a $119 list price; FeiyuTech's page states no end date.
